speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To help me narrow down the cause of these symptoms, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The acute onset of right leg weakness and falls suggests spinal cord or cauda equina compression. Given your history of forgetfulness and paranoia over the past six months, do you have any known history of multiple sclerosis, HIV, or syphilis? I will need to examine your neurological status immediately.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of acute right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and six months of progressive memory loss and paranoia in a 44-year-old male is highly concerning for a brainstem lesion or spinal cord pathology. To differentiate between a tumor, demyelination, or infection, I need to check your current neurological status and imaging.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast
